questions.q: What's the safe way to deploy an incompatible change to a Restate service in production?
options: Deploy the new version at a new endpoint, register it, and remove the old one once drained
questions.why: New invocations go to the new deployment; in-flight ones finish on the deployment they're pinned to.

questions.q: Which change is safe for running Temporal workflows WITHOUT patching?
options: Inserting a new activity call in the middle of the workflow
Changing the implementation inside an existing activity
questions.why: Activity implementations aren't replayed; only their recorded results are. Changes to the sequence of commands in workflow code are what break replay.

questions.q: Which alert would have caught incident 6.4 (silent retries) early?
options: Invocations or activities retrying for longer than N minutes
questions.why: Durable systems retry quietly. Alert on long-retrying or paused work, and on business outcomes.

questions.q: Why should secrets never be returned from a ctx.run step or an activity?
options: Step results are recorded in the journal/history, where anyone with access can read them
It isn't allowed by the SDK
questions.why: Everything journaled is durable and inspectable. Read secrets inside the step and return only what's needed.

questions.q: Which Restate SDK feature ensures only your Restate server can call your service?
questions.why: Request identity signs each request from Restate; the service rejects unsigned ones. ingressPrivate hides a handler from the ingress but is about callers through Restate.

questions.q: Three questions to ask at the start of almost every ticket are: cloud or self-hosted, which versions, and…
questions.why: Kubernetes, serverless or VMs changes how deploys, scaling and networking behave.
